definitions.definition: ell=Int.toNat(λ). When λ≥0 its integer image is λ; this equality is used only under the stated nonnegativity hypothesis.
I={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin(n), of cardinal n. Index arithmetic in factorials and binomials is natural arithmetic; for each i∈I the scalar weight ell−2i uses integer subtraction before casting.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, X_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} x^r. Products of endomorphisms mean composition, rightmost factor first.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, Y_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂
definitions.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra generated by x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r, acting on V through the given representation; these actions are X_r and Y_r.
For i∈I define e_i=Y_i v=y^i v/i!. This definition does not assert that e is a basis.
For j∈I, c_j=binom(ell,j). A bar over any integer or natural coefficient below means its image under ℤ→K.
C=∏_{j∈I} c_j; the empty product is 1.
For i∈I, d_i=∏_{j∈I,j≠i} c_j, with empty product 1.
Q=Y_ell X_ell. This is the operator called P in basis-proof.md; Q avoids conflict with the target ID P.

For i,j∈I, a_ij is the restriction of A_ij to M. Admissibility ensures that each divided-power factor preserves M and thus that this restriction exists. Superscript M on an operator denotes its restriction to M whenever preservation has been established. The existence and commutator formula for h^M are proved explicitly.

inputs.statement: ell has integer image λ and n=ell+1>0. The family e_i (i∈I) is a complex basis of V, y^{ell+1}v=0 and all higher powers of y on v vanish. For i∈I, x e_0=0; x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤ell; y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<ell; y e_ell=0; h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(ell−i+r,r)e_{i−r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤ell and is zero otherwise.
The complex-linear Chevalley operators satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h; v≠0, xv=0, hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z (equivalently under every X_r,Y_r for r≥0). M is not assumed minimal.
For every pair of natural numbers nb,kb with kb≤nb, binom(nb,kb)·kb!·(nb−kb)!=nb!.

output.statement: For each j∈I, c_j>0 and c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!, and binom(ell,ell−j)=c_j. On the complex basis e, Q e_ell=e_ell and Q e_k=0 for k<ell. For every i,j,k∈I, A_ij e_k=c_j e_i if k=j and is zero otherwise. Every A_ij preserves M and its restriction is a_ij. The following are equalities of ℤ-endomorphisms of M: for all i,j,k,l∈I, a_ij a_kl=c_j a_il if j=k, and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I} d_i a_ii=C Id_M; and C=c_i d_i for each i∈I. For every natural r, r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r. The restrictions of x,y,h exist and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M.

locals.declaration: Using the basis in N001, define E_ij to send e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero.
Let i∈I be arbitrary for the displayed identities.
Let j∈I be arbitrary for the displayed identities.
Let k∈I be arbitrary for the displayed identities.
Let l∈I be arbitrary for the displayed identities.
Let r be an arbitrary natural number.

argument.text: For every j∈I apply M005 to nb=ell,kb=j, obtaining c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!. Since ell!>0 and both factorials are positive integers, c_j>0. Apply M005 also to kb=ell−j. The two factorial products j!(ell−j)! and (ell−j)!j! coincide; cancel their positive value to get binom(ell,ell−j)=binom(ell,j)=c_j.

produces.statement: For every jj∈I, c_{jj}>0, c_{jj} jj!(ell−jj)!=ell!, and binom(ell,ell−jj)=c_{jj}.

argument.text: Using the basis e from N001 define E_ij as stated. If k<ell, X_ell e_k=0; while X_ell e_ell=e_0 and Y_ell e_0=e_ell. Thus Q=Y_ell X_ell=E_{ell,ell}. N001 also gives X_{ell−i}e_ell=e_i, its coefficient being binom(ell−i,ell−i)=1. For i,j,k∈I, compute Q Y_{ell−j}e_k. If k<j, this is killed by Q because the lowered index k+ell−j is below ell; if k>j, the Y iterate is already zero past the end of the string. If k=j, it is binom(ell,ell−j)e_ell=c_j e_ell by F001. Therefore A_ij=X_{ell−i}QY_{ell−j}=c_j E_ij on the whole complex space, since equality on a basis implies equality of linear maps.

produces.statement: Q=E_{ell,ell} and, for all ii,jj∈I, A_{ii,jj}=c_{jj} E_{ii,jj} as complex-linear maps of V.

argument.text: Evaluation on e shows E_ij E_kl=E_il if j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i E_ii=Id_V. Substitute F002: A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il if j=k and zero otherwise, since when j=k the product is c_j c_l E_il. Finite product decomposition gives C=c_i d_i for each i. Hence ∑_i d_i A_ii=∑_i C E_ii=C Id_V. By H006 every factor defining A_ij preserves M, so a_ij is its ℤ-linear restriction. For any vector of M the two sides of each integer identity have equal images in V; the inclusion M→V is injective, so the product and sum identities hold in End_ℤ(M). This restriction uses only integer coefficients, with no assertion that E preserves M and no rational scalar action on M.

produces.statement: For all ii,jj,kk,ll∈I, A_{ii,jj} preserves M, a_{ii,jj} a_{kk,ll}=c_{jj} a_{ii,ll} for jj=kk and zero otherwise, C=c_{ii} d_{ii}, and ∑_{ss∈I}d_ss a_{ss,ss}=C Id_M.

argument.text: For every natural r, definitions give r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r in End_ℂ(V), since r! is nonzero in ℂ. H006 ensures all these maps preserve M, including X_1=x and Y_1=y. Restricting the equalities through the injective inclusion gives r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r on M. H005 gives h=xy−yx, so h preserves M and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M. With F001–F003 these prove all statements of the output. When ell=0, I has the single member 0, 0!=1, c_0=C=d_0=1, and Q=A_00=Id_V by the basis computation; all corresponding lattice identities remain valid.

applications.bindings: nb=ell, kb=j and kb=ell−j, for each j∈I.
hypothesis_checks: j≤ell by I, and ell−j≤ell by natural subtraction.
